hints: There are only three possible values. Could you sort them in a single pass by sending 0s to the front and 2s to the back as you meet them?
Keep three pointers: low (next spot for a 0), mid (current element) and high (next spot for a 2). This is the Dutch National Flag partition.

1. Set low = 0, mid = 0, high = n-1.
  2. While mid <= high: if flags[mid] is 0, swap it with flags[low], then move both low and mid forward.
  3. If it is 1, just move mid forward.
  4. If it is 2, swap it with flags[high] and move high back (do not move mid, the swapped-in value is unchecked).

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Count how many 0s, 1s and 2s there are, then overwrite the array with that many of each (two passes).

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One-pass three-pointer partition that swaps 0s to the front and 2s to the back.

explain: For [2,1,0,2,0,1,1]: mid sees 2, swaps with the last element (1), high shrinks; mid sees that 1 and moves on; and so on. At every moment [0, low) holds only 0s, [low, mid) only 1s, and (high, n-1] only 2s, while [mid, high] is still unknown. The loop ends when the unknown part is empty, giving [0,0,1,1,1,2,2]. The classic bug is advancing mid after swapping with high; the incoming value has not been looked at yet.
recognize: Sort an array with only a few distinct values in place, in one pass → three-pointer partition.
